approval_evidence.quote: We have approved your BLA for aflibercept effective this date. [November 18, 2011] ... Aflibercept is indicated for treatment of neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration.

notes: Regeneron books U.S. net product sales; Bayer HealthCare books ex-U.S. (the releases also print an EYLEA global/Total column, not used). From 2023Q3 Regeneron prints EYLEA HD on its own line; the series is the EYLEA (2 mg) line only, and EYLEA HD did not exist before 2023Q3, so the line keeps the same definition throughout. For 2024Q1-2024Q4 the detail table in each release prints a combined 'EYLEA HD and EYLEA' row, so those four quarters use the summary line 'EYLEA - U.S.' (whole millions) from the quarter's own release; the 2025 releases' prior-year columns give EYLEA alone with decimals and agree within rounding. Quarters 2011Q4-2013Q3 are press-release sentences (whole millions, 24.8 for 2011Q4) because those releases print no EYLEA-only table row.
search_log: Pulled data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000872589.json plus CIK0000872589-submissions-001.json (older pages) and listed every 8-K, 8-K/A, 10-Q, 10-K from 2011-06 on (script scripts/list.py); the listing kept all 8-K and 8-K/A with Item 2.02 and did not filter by form beyond that. No 8-K/A with Item 2.02 appears in the listing.

Fetched each Item 2.02 8-K's filing index.json (scripts/idx.py) and downloaded every EX-99.x exhibit (scripts/fetch.py); one earnings release per quarter was used; January JPM-conference decks and the 2023-2026 Apr/Jul/Oct preannouncement 8-Ks carry no product table and were not used.

Rows were extracted from the cached exhibits by scripts/build.py (table cells, percentage-change columns dropped) and checked with scripts/sourcing/verify_staged_manifests.py (0 failures at write time).
Cross-checks run: prior-year columns of the following year's release vs this series' own values; sum of four quarters vs the full-year figure the releases print.
Full-text/approval: FDA approval letter BLA 125387 dated 2011-11-18 fetched from accessdata.fda.gov and read.
